source.authors: José Augusto Pereira Carneiro Muniz, Luana Modesto de Athaide, Bruno Duarte Gomes, Barbara L. Finlay, Luiz Carlos de Lima Silveira
source.title: Ganglion Cell and Displaced Amacrine Cell Density Distribution in the Retina of the Howler Monkey (Alouatta caraya)

where: Results, Ganglion cell density along the horizontal and vertical meridians of the Alouatta retina
method: Nissl-stained (cresyl violet) flat-mounted retinas; ganglion cells counted by light microscopy along 12 radial directions from the fovea
conditions: Five adult male Alouatta caraya from the breeding colony of the Centro Nacional de Primatas (Ananindeua, Para, Brazil), bred and kept in the colony until the experiment (captive-bred, not wild); ages not reported. Six flat-mounted retinas (left retinas of four animals, both retinas of the fifth); five counted over their whole extent and a sixth only in midperipheral and peripheral regions. The means and standard deviations for the central 3 mm are plotted for N = 5 retinas (preceding Results sentence). Cells counted along 12 radial directions at 30 degree intervals from the fovea with a 100x oil objective, sampling every 0.25 mm for the first 3 mm; counting fields 1,537 square micrometres to 1.5 mm. Retinas fixed (10% formaldehyde perfusion) then exposed to formaldehyde vapour at 60 C; areal shrinkage in four retinas averaged 4.8 +/- 4.3% (range 1 to 11%) and no correction was applied to densities, so densities are for shrunken tissue. Values are mean +/- SD: nasal 44,963 +/- 3,089; temporal 42,191 +/- 2,063; dorsal 43,825 +/- 788; ventral 40,673 +/- 2,669. The abstract states the peak as 'reaching 40,700-45,200 cells/mm2' at 0.5 mm 'between the fovea and optic nerve head', slightly different from the Results means (upper figure 45,200 versus 44,963; the Results give four named directions, the abstract does not). No acuity (cycles per degree) estimate is reported in the paper. Density is for ganglion cells; displaced amacrine cells are counted separately (peaks 2,050 to 3,100 cells/mm2 in the abstract).
quote: Ganglion cell density reached maximum values in the foveal slope: 44,963±3,089, 42,191±2,063, 43,825±788, and 40,673±2,669 cells/mm2 at 0.5 mm nasal, temporal, dorsal, and ventral to the fovea, respectively.

Trait key peak_ganglion_cell_density_mm2 as used on main (new trait for this species). source.title: Migratory blackcaps can use their magnetic compass at 5 degrees inclination, but are completely random at 0 degrees inclination

method: orientation tests of caged night-migratory birds in Faraday-shielded huts under controlled magnetic fields, inclination 67 (local), 5 and 0 degrees, horizontal component pointing to magnetic north (NMF) or rotated -120 degrees (CMF); Rayleigh tests
value: oriented at 5 degrees inclination as well as in the normal 67 degree inclined field (Oldenburg)
quote: At 5° inclination, the birds oriented as well as they did in the normal 67° inclined field in Oldenburg.
conditions: Wild-caught Eurasian blackcaps (August 2013 and 2014, within 1 km of the University of Oldenburg, Germany), housed indoors under local photoperiod; 26 birds in total (summarising page tool). Groups and N per condition as printed: spring 2014 5 deg NMF N = 11, 5 deg CMF N = 11, 0 deg NMF N = 11, 0 deg CMF N = 12; autumn 2014 67 deg NMF N = 11, 5 deg NMF N = 10, 5 deg CMF N = 9 (0 deg omitted in autumn); spring 2015 67 deg NMF and CMF N = 13 each, 0 deg NMF N = 9, 0 deg CMF N = 12. Rayleigh tests, birds tested in a field with fluxgate monitoring (tool summary: control and 0 deg tests semi-randomly intermixed; evaluators blind to the direction in a double-blind replication; about 25% of nights classed inactive and excluded). Sex and age not read. Stimulus is a set (nominal) inclination, with field strength held constant (tool summary), not a separately reported measured value. 5 deg results (Results, Rayleigh): spring 2014 5 deg NMF mean 47 deg, r = 0.61, N = 11, p < 0.05; 5 deg CMF mean 294 deg, r = 0.57, N = 11, p < 0.05 (turned accordingly after the -120 deg rotation); autumn 2014 67 deg NMF 235 deg, r = 0.55, N = 11, p < 0.05; 5 deg NMF 204 deg, r = 0.57, N = 10, p < 0.05; 5 deg CMF 78 deg, r = 0.73, N = 9, p < 0.01; spring 2015 67 deg NMF 38 deg, r = 0.66, N = 13, p < 0.01; 67 deg CMF 284 deg, r = 0.79, N = 13, p < 0.001. Contrary result for the same birds: at 0 deg inclination orientation was random in every condition (companion record).
note: Whole abstract sentence of 19 words (abstract read in consecutive pieces; this sentence returned unbroken on two passes). Not on main under this DOI; main holds other Sylvia atricapilla sense_magnetic rows (radio-noise papers, different DOIs). value: randomly oriented in the horizontal field (0 degrees inclination), no sign of bimodality
quote: In contrast, they were completely randomly oriented in the horizontal field, showing no sign of bimodality.
conditions: Wild-caught Eurasian blackcaps (August 2013 and 2014, within 1 km of the University of Oldenburg, Germany), housed indoors under local photoperiod; 26 birds in total (summarising page tool). Groups and N per condition as printed: spring 2014 5 deg NMF N = 11, 5 deg CMF N = 11, 0 deg NMF N = 11, 0 deg CMF N = 12; autumn 2014 67 deg NMF N = 11, 5 deg NMF N = 10, 5 deg CMF N = 9 (0 deg omitted in autumn); spring 2015 67 deg NMF and CMF N = 13 each, 0 deg NMF N = 9, 0 deg CMF N = 12. Sex and age not read. Stimulus is a set (nominal) inclination, with field strength held constant (tool summary), not a separately reported measured value. Null result. 0 deg results (Rayleigh): spring 2014 0 deg NMF mean 16 deg, r = 0.26, p = 0.486 (ns), N = 11; 0 deg CMF mean 360 deg, r = 0.36, p = 0.214 (ns), N = 12; spring 2015 0 deg NMF mean 8 deg, r = 0.2, p = 0.709 (ns), N = 9; 0 deg CMF mean 143 deg, r = 0.08, p > 0.9 (ns), N = 12; pooled 0 deg NMF over spring 2014-2015 mean 25 deg, r = 0.33, p = 0.140 (ns), N = 17. value: with the oscillating-field device switched on, birds were not disoriented and showed autumn-appropriate migratory orientation (mean 189 deg, n = 14, r = 0.49, P = 0.03)

source.authors: Julia Bojarinova, Kirill Kavokin, Alexander Pakhomov, Roman Cherbunin, Anna Anashina, Maria Erokhina, Maria Ershova, Nikita Chernetsov
source.title: Magnetic compass of garden warblers is not affected by oscillating magnetic fields applied to their eyes

method: Emlen funnel orientation tests of caged night-migratory birds in a screened non-magnetic chamber, with a portable coil device generating an oscillating magnetic field (OMF, about 5 nT) at the eyes, switched on or off; Rayleigh tests
conditions: First-year garden warblers captured wild during autumn migration on the Courish Spit, Kaliningrad region, Russia; held in individual outdoor cages at least 5 days; birds with nocturnal restlessness selected; tested 23 August to 16 September, 50 min from astronomical twilight (details from a summarising page tool). Phase 1, no device, indoors: n = 21, r = 0.38, P = 0.045. Switched-off device (dummy of equal weight): alpha = 164 deg, n = 11, r = 0.51, P = 0.056, just below the significance level (so the off-device control group itself was not significantly oriented). Switched-on device: n = 14 (the quoted result). Contrary result: the same species placed in a homogeneous 5 nT OMF from large stationary coils (no device, n = 12, r = 0.11, P = 0.86) showed clear disorientation. Of 22 birds fitted with devices, 21 were active. Device tests double-blind until all experiments ended; birds with fewer than 40 scratches or judged disoriented were excluded; Rayleigh tests at 5%. The order of test conditions is not described; the OMF strength was nominal 5 nT, checked before and after tests with a ferrite antenna and oscilloscope (summary). The two device groups (on and off) were different birds as far as the page summary shows (not confirmed).
quote: Extraordinarily, when the device was on, they were not disoriented either: the birds showed migratory orientation appropriate for autumn migratory season (α = 189°, n = 14, r = 0.49, P = 0.03; Fig. 2D).
note: Whole Results sentence of 31 words, read in two abutting pieces in one response and again with the same join on a second response (said in pieces). The abstract sentence 'Surprisingly, the birds were not disoriented and showed the seasonally appropriate migratory direction.' reports the same result. Null-type finding: the authors read it as showing the oscillating-field effect on the eye is absent for the magnetic compass here. Not on main under this DOI or species+sense_magnetic (main holds only visual rows for Sylvia borin). Family and order as on main (Sylviidae, Passeriformes); Sylvia borin not listed in gbif-names.tsv, name as used on main. value: control birds kept without natural celestial cues remained unable to orient in the geomagnetic field

source.authors: Bianca Alert, Andreas Michalik, Nadine Thiele, Michael Bottesch, Henrik Mouritsen
source.title: Re-calibration of the magnetic compass in hand-raised European robins (Erithacus rubecula)

method: Emlen funnel orientation tests in aluminium-shielded huts in a simulated geomagnetic field (48,880 nT, 67.5 deg inclination, 0 deg declination); Rayleigh tests; hand-raised birds with or without exposure to natural celestial cues
conditions: 41 nestlings taken from nests near Oldenburg, Lower Saxony, Germany, at 5 to 11 days old (13 in 2010, 13 in 2011, 15 in 2013), hand-raised in a windowless room with a lamp-simulated photoperiod and the geomagnetic field but no natural celestial cues (wild-origin nestlings, hand-raised captive adults). Autumn baseline, all 41 birds in the normal geomagnetic field: not significantly oriented (Rayleigh mean 23 deg, r = 0.17, n = 41, P = 0.295). At the end of February about half were moved to an outdoor aviary with natural celestial cues (experimental, n = 22: 7 in 2011, 6 in 2012, 9 in 2014) and the rest stayed indoors (control, n = 19); the paper does not describe how birds were assigned. Spring tests mid-March to mid-April, one hour, once or twice, up to nine birds per night, both groups mostly tested simultaneously; of 547 spring tests 130 were excluded for low activity, 12 for bimodal and 45 for random orientation; two scorers, a third re-analysed differences over 30 deg (all from a summarising page tool). Control spring result (Results): Rayleigh mean 294 deg, r = 0.08, n = 19, P = 0.895 (disoriented). Contrary comparison: the experimental group oriented in the north-easterly spring direction (mean 56 deg, r = 0.43, n = 22); the Results text prints P = 0.004 but the Fig. 2 caption prints P = 0.017 for the same group, a discrepancy in the paper. Randomisation and handler blinding to group are not described.
quote: In contrast, control birds that were deprived of any natural celestial cues throughout remained unable to orient.
note: Whole abstract sentence of 17 words, returned unbroken on two passes (the sentence before it says birds with celestial-cue access could orient in the spring direction). Null result for the control group. Not on main under this DOI. Family and order (Muscicapidae, Passeriformes) as on main for this species; GBIF ACCEPTED in gbif-names.tsv; main's other Erithacus rubecula sense_magnetic rows have different DOIs (pone.0043271, the bpj paper).
